title: CPOM Antarctic surface elevation change rate, 1995-2026, multi-mission radar altimetry
product_version: CPOM multi-mission radar altimetry surface elevation change, Antarctica, 5 km, product version 1.0 (fv1)
reference: Shepherd, A. et al. (2019): Trends in Antarctic Ice Sheet elevation and mass. Geophysical Research Letters 46, 8174-8183. doi:10.1029/2019GL082182
license: CC BY 4.0 (the CPOM files' licence); cite the sources listed under `sources`

dataset.citation: Centre for Polar Observation and Modelling (2026): Antarctic Ice Sheet surface elevation change at 5 km from multi-mission radar altimetry (ERS-2, Envisat, CryoSat-2), product version 1.0. CPOM Land Ice Portal.
dataset.creators: A. Muir, T. Slater, J. Maddalena, B. Palmer (CPOM)

paper.citation: Shepherd, A. et al. (2019): Trends in Antarctic Ice Sheet elevation and mass. Geophysical Research Letters 46, 8174-8183.

sources.missions: ERS-2 and Envisat (ESA FDR4ALT Land Ice Thematic Data Product v1) and CryoSat-2 (ESA Cryo-TEMPO Land Ice, Baseline D)

resampling.method: area-weighted mean of the 5 km CPOM cells overlapping each explorer cell
resampling.drawn_on: explorer ice cells (BedMachine Antarctica v4 grounded ice, floating ice and Lake Vostok)
resampling.reason: CPOM's cells are on a 5 km EPSG:3031 grid of their own; overlay and terrain cells must correspond one to one
resampling.rows: CPOM rows run south to north and are flipped

period.note: linear trend of the cross-calibrated, gap-filled elevation record over the period

pole_hole.note: south of 88 S the rate is extrapolated throughout; south of 81.5 S so are its years before CryoSat-2 data arrive, late in 2010

validation.note: volume-change rate (grid area, no map-scale correction) of the CPOM 5 km field and of the packed cells: net, and over the thickening and the thinning cells. They differ where CPOM cells fall outside explorer ice or below the cover threshold, and averaging cancels opposite-signed rates within a cell

fields.name: basin_id
fields.note: IMBIE drainage basins, numbered, named and cited (Rignot et al., 2016) as in CPOM's basin_id; each cell takes the basin of the CPOM cell under its centre
